deck.audience: public health professionals and policy analysts reviewing vaccination impact and progress

brief.title: The Power of Vaccination: From Smallpox Eradication to COVID-19 in Record Time
brief.one_liner: A data-driven overview of how vaccines have transformed public health by eliminating or drastically reducing deadly diseases over the past two centuries.
brief.goal: Audience should understand the historical trajectory of vaccine development, quantify the dramatic reductions in disease burden vaccines have achieved, and recognize remaining challenges in global vaccination coverage.

slides.title: The Power of Vaccination: From Smallpox Eradication to COVID-19 in Record Time
slides.objective: Cover slide with deck title, subtitle summarizing scope (1796–2020), and source attribution to Our World in Data.

slides.title: From 100 Years to Under 1 Year: Vaccine Development Is Accelerating
slides.objective: Show the timeline from pathogen identification to vaccine licensure for key diseases. Use a horizontal bar/timeline chart referencing the vaccination innovation figure. Highlight that early vaccines took decades (typhoid: 105 years) while COVID-19 took under 1 year.

slides.title: 100% Case Reduction Achieved for Diphtheria, Polio, and Smallpox in the US
slides.objective: Present a table or data visualization showing pre-vaccine vs. post-vaccine case and death rates for major diseases in the US. Emphasize the diseases with 100% reduction and those still with remaining burden (pneumococcal, hepatitis).

slides.title: Measles Cases Collapsed Across All 50 US States After Vaccine Mandates
slides.objective: Display the measles heatmap showing state-by-state case rates from 1929–2022, with annotations for the 1963 vaccine, 1971 MMR, and 1980 mandate. Illustrate the dramatic shift from high incidence (100–1,000+ cases per 100,000) before 1963 to near zero after the 1980 mandate, with only sporadic outbreaks.

slides.title: Smallpox: The Only Human Disease Eradicated Through Vaccination
slides.objective: Narrate the smallpox eradication timeline — from WHO resolution in 1959 to the last case in 1977 and certification in 1980. Use the endemic countries chart. Explain why smallpox was uniquely suited for eradication.

slides.title: Herd Immunity: How Vaccinating Many Protects the Most Vulnerable
slides.objective: Explain the concept of herd immunity with a clear visual or diagram. Note that vaccines protect not just individuals but also newborns, immunocompromised patients, and those on chemotherapy who cannot be vaccinated.

slides.title: Gaps Persist: Pneumococcal Disease Shows Only 40% Case Reduction
slides.objective: Highlight diseases where vaccine impact is still incomplete — pneumococcal disease (40.5% case reduction, 31.3% death reduction), hepatitis A (89%), and acute hepatitis B (83.9%). Discuss access gaps, supply shortages, and trust challenges as barriers.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: Vaccines Have Eliminated Deadly Diseases — But the Job Isn't Done
slides.objective: Summarize 4–5 key findings: vaccines achieved 100% elimination of multiple diseases in the US, development timelines have collapsed from over 100 years to under 1 year, herd immunity protects entire communities, but coverage gaps persist for diseases like pneumococcal disease, hepatitis A, and hepatitis B. End with a forward-looking call to improve access, coverage, and trust in vaccination.
